description: I'm an Aerospace Engineering student passionate about human spaceflight, astronaut health, and space research. I'm looking for enthusiastic teammates skilled in Python, AI/ML, data analysis, software development, or UI/UX. If you're passionate about space and would love to collaborate on an innovative solution for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, I'd be happy to have you on my team. Let's build something impactful together!
summary:
Astronauts experience complex physiological, cognitive and physical changes during spaceflight. Monitoring these aspects independently may not provide a complete picture of their overall health. Project ASTRON addresses this challenge through an integrated health monitoring platform that brings together three key assessment systems: wearable-based physiological monitoring, interactive cognitive assessment and camera-based movement analysis.

The system tracks vital parameters such as heart rate, SpO₂, blood pressure, skin temperature and sleep duration, evaluates cognitive functions through interactive games, and analyses body posture and joint movements using computer vision. These outputs are presented through a unified dashboard, enabling multiple aspects of astronaut health to be assessed within a single platform.

By combining these different dimensions of health monitoring, Project ASTRON aims to move beyond isolated health measurements towards a more comprehensive understanding of astronaut well-being during space missions.
details:
Project ASTRON is an integrated Astronaut Health Monitoring System developed to assess three interconnected aspects of astronaut well-being: physiological health, cognitive performance and physical movement.

The system consists of three major modules:

1. Physiological Monitoring: This module provides a wearable monitoring interface to track heart rate, SpO₂, blood pressure, skin temperature and sleep duration. MATLAB is used to generate and process simulated physiological readings for demonstration and testing. The team has also explored NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), particularly the SpaceX Inspiration4 dataset (OSD-575), to identify relevant physiological research data.

2. Cognitive Assessment: This module incorporates interactive games designed to assess memory, attention, concentration and reaction time. These assessments provide a way to observe changes in cognitive performance through task-based interactions.

3. Movement Analysis: This module uses camera-based body tracking developed with Python and Google's MediaPipe. It detects body landmarks, generates skeletal connections and calculates selected joint angles, including elbow and knee angles, to analyse posture and movement.

All three modules are brought together through a unified dashboard that presents monitoring outputs and assessment results in an accessible visual format.

Technology Stack: Python, MATLAB, Google MediaPipe and dashboard-based data visualisation.

Innovation and Impact: Unlike conventional monitoring approaches that focus primarily on individual physiological measurements, Project ASTRON combines physiological, cognitive and movement assessments within one platform. This integrated approach aims to provide a broader understanding of astronaut health and support the identification of potential changes across different aspects of well-being during space missions.

The final prototype demonstrates the integration of these three monitoring capabilities and provides a foundation for further validation and development.
